name: Ecosia Browser
businessModel: Search advertising revenue share (Yahoo and Microsoft Advertising) and shopping affiliate links; profits fund tree planting and renewable energy
statusNote: Desktop launched Apr 22, 2024 (mobile apps replaced earlier Ecosia search apps); Linux build added Sept 2026
pitch: Chromium browser built around Ecosia search, with a built-in ad blocker and tree counter.
summary: Chrome-like browser from the Berlin search company Ecosia, with built-in ad and tracker blocking, Ecosia search and AI Chat. Closed source; revenue from search ads and shopping affiliate links funds tree planting.
bestFor: Ecosia search users who want one app for search and browsing
Chrome users who want a similar browser with built-in blocking
People who like a company that publishes monthly finances and plants trees
Europeans who prefer a German GDPR-bound provider
notFor: Anyone who wants an open-source browser
Privacy-first users who want strict defaults and fingerprint resistance
People who dislike affiliate shopping links and sponsored placements

pros.title: Built-in ad and tracker blocker
pros.detail: EasyList and EasyPrivacy-style lists plus cookie-consent handling and social-embed toggles, without extensions.

pros.title: Chromium compatibility
pros.detail: Chrome Web Store extensions and near-Chrome site compatibility on Windows, macOS and Linux.

pros.title: Chrome-style resource savers
pros.detail: Memory Saver and Energy Saver are reported alongside tab previews.

pros.title: Transparent funding
pros.detail: B Corp since 2014, with shares held so the owners cannot sell it or take profits, and monthly published finances.

pros.title: Easy import
pros.detail: Imports history, favorites, passwords and autofill data from other browsers.

cons.title: Closed source
cons.detail: The Register confirms Ecosia's browsers are not open source despite the open-source Chromium base.

cons.title: Affiliate links
cons.detail: Shopping links to Amazon, eBay and Decathlon feed Ecosia revenue, which some users dislike.

cons.title: Data defaults
cons.detail: Anonymous usage and crash data is sent by default and must be switched off; blocking is a setting to enable.

cons.title: Thin differentiation
cons.detail: Reviews describe a fairly standard Chromium experience with little beyond Ecosia branding and widgets.

faq.q: Does Ecosia make its own browser?
faq.a: Yes. Ecosia launched a Chromium-based browser for Windows and macOS on Apr 22, 2024, alongside Android and iOS apps, and added Linux in Sept 2026.

faq.q: Is the Ecosia browser open source?
faq.a: No. It is built on open-source Chromium but Ecosia's own browsers are proprietary.

It started on OpenAI's API, and the Wikipedia article reports a switch to a small Mistral model in May 2026. One October 2026 report about adopting open models, including Chinese ones, is unconfirmed.

timeline.event: Cross-platform browser launched for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android (Apr 22)

switching.note: Settings > You and Ecosia Browser imports from other browsers or profiles; the import can be repeated.

sync.note: No sync documented in the sources reviewed (unverified)

mv2.note: Chromium base; the Chrome Web Store dropped MV2 in 2026

ai.note: Ecosia AI Chat; no global off switch documented

privacy.defaults: Ad and tracker blocking, anti-fingerprinting and third-party cookie blocking exist as settings; default state not confirmed
privacy.telemetry: Anonymous usage and crash reports sent by default, can be turned off in Settings > Privacy and security

spec.telemetry: Anonymous usage and crash data, opt-out
spec.patchLag: Not published; listing shows Chromium 152 on Sept 7, 2026

telemetryOptOut: Usage and crash data can be turned off
adBlocker: EasyList, EasyPrivacy and some uBO filters
cookieBanners: Auto cookie manager, not always successful
aiKillSwitch: Separate Ecosia feature; no global switch documented

memory: Chromium base; Memory Saver and ad blocking help
resourceControls: Memory Saver and Energy Saver reported
privacyDefaults: Blocker present but a setting; telemetry on by default
blocking: EasyList, EasyPrivacy, some uBO lists; no custom lists
fingerprinting: Simple property randomization, may break sites
patchSpeed: Chromium 152 on Sept 7; update cadence unpublished
telemetry: Anonymous usage data on by default, opt-out
searchFreedom: Ecosia pushed, engines can be changed
productivity: AI Chat and widgets, little else
extras: Tree counter, climate ratings, AI Chat
mobileApps: Android and iOS apps, no extensions
businessTrust: B Corp, monthly finances, but affiliate links
longevity: Funded by search revenue; expanding to Linux
